definition: A way of separating a mixture. Each component is carried along by a moving phase and held back by a fixed phase, through intermolecular forces, so components that are held back less travel further.
The phase that moves through or over the stationary phase and carries the components with it, such as the liquid solvent in paper chromatography or TLC.
The phase that stays fixed and holds components back by attracting them, such as the silica layer on a TLC plate or the water held in the fibres of chromatography paper.
$R_\text{F}$: the distance a component moves from the baseline divided by the distance the solvent front moves from the baseline. It has no units and lies between 0 and 1.
